analysis.title: Extreme markets: welcome to maximum pain
key_insights: SPX futures printed a large hammer after an aggressive overnight selloff and reclaimed the range in place since August. Overnight lows came close to the 200-day moving average.
SPX is roughly flat since May with no medium-term trend. The note says chasing momentum at range extremes has lost money and mean reversion has been the required approach.
Goldman's trading desk sees a rotation inside tech: hyperscalers outperform by 350bps while semiconductors lag by 250bps as investors use them as a source of funds.
Goldman's desk reasons that restrictions on data center expansion could make existing compute more valuable, supporting pricing power, lowering capex needs and freeing cash for buybacks.
AI Leaders are down 500bps, power-related stocks down 600bps and data centers down 540bps. The market is separating AI infrastructure beneficiaries from those funding the buildout.

Goldman's Callahan notes semiconductor forward P/E fell more than 40% in two months, from 28x to 16x. The SOX trades at about a 2-turn forward P/E discount to the S&P 500, near the widest gap in 15 years.
Semiconductor volatility (VXSMH) has barely moved while the VIX is falling, leaving a large gap between the two. The note says this is not what a healthy recovery looks like.

JPMorgan says memory stocks are down 45% from their 2026 peak versus a 29% drawdown for the SOX. SK Hynix is down 53% from its highs and Samsung down 40%. The market moved from pricing an AI supercycle to pricing a memory downturn.

JPMorgan Market Intelligence says the S&P 500 has averaged gains of 5.4%, 11.4%, 12.5% and 14.7% over 3, 6, 9 and 12 months after US midterms since 1990, with a 100% positive hit rate at 6, 9 and 12 months.

JPMorgan argues the recent de-risking is not fully capitulatory, with quant selling and elevated tech positioning still risks. Momentum exposure has fallen to 30% of its peak and deleveraging has been widespread.
Morgan Stanley's Composite Sentiment Indicator is approaching the panic zone but has not reached the -2.00 flush. The note says markets do not necessarily need full capitulation to squeeze.

JPMorgan cites two regulatory meetings on November 2 aimed at stabilizing Chinese equities, including expanded capital-market support tools and better buyback financing, plus signs of government-backed buying. It sees an emerging policy floor but needs sustained inflows to confirm a bottom.
Brent is in its worst four-day selloff since the 2020 COVID crash.
Goldman says CTA downside convexity in oil is large. Stops have triggered, but much of the systematic selling may not yet be executed, so forced liquidation could add pressure.
